Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):
  • Acute flare-up of asthma with wheeze, cough, dyspnea × 2–3 days  
  • History of childhood and adult asthma, hay fever (allergic rhinitis), and eczema  
  • No chest pain, hemoptysis, or nocturnal symptoms reported  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes): Not recorded.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  
  • Salbutamol inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented (used every few weeks and before exercise)  
  • No regular hay-fever medication; none other reported  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus): Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks: Not recorded.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  
  • Physical activity: normally walks to work; currently limited due to breathlessness  
  • Tobacco: non-smoker  
  • Alcohol: ~1 glass of wine every 2–3 days  
  • Other substances: Not recorded  
  • Diet: Not recorded  
- Hearing and vision concerns: Not recorded.  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm): Not recorded.  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:  
  • Lives with partner  
  • Employed as an engineer; currently working from home or on sick leave due to symptoms  
  • Other social or financial issues: Not recorded  

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded. (Patient-reported temperature 37 °C)  
- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated: Not recorded.  
- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant: Not recorded.  
- Ear exam including otoscopy: Not recorded.  
- Eye exam: visual acuity, pupil response, fundus if indicated: Not recorded.  
- Urinalysis: dipstick for protein, glucose, ketones, blood: Not recorded.  

Investigations (as indicated)

- Peak flow monitoring: peak flow meter prescribed; patient to record morning and evening readings for 1 week  
- Blood tests: Not ordered.  
- Renal and liver function tests: Not ordered.  
- ECG: Not ordered.  
- Cancer screening (cervical, breast, bowel): Not recorded.  
- Bone density: Not recorded.  

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification  
  • Advised to use salbutamol 2–4 puffs via spacer every 4 hours initially  
  • Counseled on monitoring symptoms and seeking care if fever or wheeze worsens  
  • Advised to commence regular OTC antihistamine for allergic component  
- Discuss patient health goals and priorities: Improve breathing control; return to normal activity.  
- Assess eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA): Not discussed.  
- Referral to allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports: Not discussed.  
- Schedule follow-up and recall appointments as needed: Review in 1 week or sooner if deterioration.  

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral: Consider if chronic disease impacts wellbeing.  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management: Respiratory specialist review if poor control.  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified: Not indicated from current consult.  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening: Not indicated from current consult.  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected: Not indicated.  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health: Not indicated.  

Quality checks

● Missing but clinically expected elements: BP, pulse, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, height/weight/BMI, waist circumference, immunisation history, comprehensive lifestyle assessment, mood screening, family history of chronic disease, urinalysis, blood tests for chronic disease screening (e.g., fasting glucose, lipids).  
● Internal conflicts or contradictions: None noted.  
● Transcript quality notes: Audio clear; limited data gathered on preventive health domains because consult focused on acute asthma flare.
